english_verification.review_scope: Representative names, opening identity, source prose and actual fixed-revision Wiki passages, plus native national-idea text compared by localisation key. Large mission/idea ranges are locator envelopes, not exhaustive checks of every intervening line or runtime reachability.
unresolved: Mission reachability and every effect were not exhaustively audited.
No formal validator, test, build, website generation, map generation, Chinese-source, scoring, commit, or push was performed.
Original Chinese transliterations are rendered using current Mod names Moguwon Wolfborn and Kitokan Boarborn; setting futures remain attributed historical material, not guaranteed EU4 outcomes.

rationale.campaign_length: The current 215 direct missions and 25 regional campaigns span the entire game.
rationale.colonization: No confirmed core gameplay loop centres on overseas colonisation.
rationale.complexity: Campaign selection, estate loyalty, subjects, Korashi, governing capacity and disaster preparation must be managed together.
rationale.dark_story: Enslavement, assimilation, anti-magic persecution and military hierarchy are core institutions, not background decoration.
rationale.difficulty: Defeating neighbours is usually not the main challenge; sustaining a very long conquest schedule and preparing for disasters are.
rationale.diplomacy: Allies, subjects and estates matter, but diplomacy ultimately serves conquest and internal power balances.
rationale.early_pressure: A strong starting base still requires handling unrest, mines and resource supply; pressure is lower than survival as a weak state.
rationale.magic_artifice_intensity: Anti-magic material, suppression of shamans and magical disasters dominate: the focus is controlling magic, not becoming a spellcasting state.
rationale.narrative_density: The military alliance, imperial reforms, Wuhyunisation, six-Command tensions and two disasters form a continuous national transformation.
rationale.tall_play: Administrative and mining development support expansion, while the endgame demands extensive territory and cultural transformation.
rationale.trade_economy: The Jade Mines, subjects and continental trade support warfare, but economics is not the primary national fantasy.
rationale.warfare: The war room, 25 regional campaigns, dedicated Commands and continental conquest make warfare central throughout.

identity.appearance: A directly selectable hobgoblin military state in 1444, built around the Wolf, Boar and Lion Commands and ruling four slave subject states.

national_ideas.scope_note: National traditions, seven national ideas and ambition only; racial, government and optional idea-group bonuses are excluded. Conditional alternatives are listed separately, not stacked; accepting new ideas on formation depends on the actual event/decision and player choice.

description.text: In the aftermath of our invasion of northern Rahen, we had to quickly adapt our administration to accommodate the new territories. Many local leaders organised resistance against our rule, which weakened our control over the conquered lands. In response we hunted them down and executed them. We ensured that they were replaced with weaker willed locals. These meek rulers would lead by example. Under the watchful eye of hobgoblin garrisons they greatly weakened any resistance to our rule. It was through these strict measures that newly conquered peoples and lands could be quickly incorporated into our Great Command as we marched upon Haless.

description.text: Through many generations we have developed traditional techniques of drilling our armies. While these techniques had been adequate for border protection and the conquest of the Jade Mines, our expansion into northern Haless introduced us to several new enemies. This kick-started the development of modernised drills. The two main drills were those developed by the Wolf Command, which centered around cavalry flanking maneuvers, and those developed by the Boar command, which centered around massed infantry. The latter of the two would prove a very effective baseline for later firearm drills.

description.text: Constant warfare both within and outside of the Jade Mines has pushed hobgoblin society into ever greater centralisation and militarisation in the form of various Commands, culminating in the founding of the Great Command in 1391 AA. This has led to hobgoblin society becoming an incredibly well oiled machine capable of supplying vast armies with extreme efficiency, with almost every household capable of producing weapons, uniforms and soldiers for the Great Command’s endless campaigns. This has resulted in a civil society that is completely integrated into the purpose of the state: War.

description.text: Honour is a core pillar of our culture. And honour is kept through loyalty. No good hobgoblin would even consider betraying their duty to their family and Command and lose their honour. A hobgoblin without honour loses their family, their position, their very place in society. They are removed from all the things that give meaning to life and thus often end up with two options, suicide or exile. Suicide is the preferred choice for those who have dishonoured themselves, for such is the weight of our honour. No secrets are spilled.

description.text: As the armies of the Wolf, Boar and Lion grew in size and strength, various Grand Marshals of the Great Command sought to expand the forces directly controlled by them beyond the enslaved Zanyu Kikun. This led to the creation and steady expansion of the Ninyu Kikun, the combined army, which answered only to the Grand Marshal. This force would systematically recruit the most disciplined soldiers and most accomplished commanders into the service of the Grand Marshal, eventually forming the most formidable army of the Command. The Ninyu Kikun would be the first of the armies to adopt artillery into their formations, crushing enemy defences and opposition while paving the way for the artillery innovations of the Dragon Command. The existence of the Ninyu Kikun also served to increase the authority and control of the Grand Marshal within the military structures of the Command and by extension their authority over the lesser Marshals.

description.text: Hobgoblin military education begins in the family, with grandfathers and fathers beginning the process of passing down their martial skills to their sons from the age of 8. Years of training from a young age form the foundation that a young hobgoblin builds upon through their introduction into larger military divisions, such as a senun, banner, or ten, regiment. It is here that a hobgoblin has the opportunity to distinguish themselves on the battlefield, potentially earning an exaltation from a superior officer. A hobgoblin soldier who earns themselves an exaltation is given an advanced military education and promoted to captain, regardless of their clan’s status. The system of exaltations ensures that the officer corps of the Command has greater pools of talents to draw upon than most states on Halann and prevents the elite clans from monopolising leadership positions.

description.text: Our expansion outside of Shamakhad began to strain the administration due to the lack of loyal and honourable hobgoblins to govern our newly conquered lands. This led to our Grand Marshal dividing the three original Commands into the Tiger, Elephant and Dragon commands, who would found war camps and settle in the lands outside of Shamakhad. The influx of our people into the distant territories allowed for the expansion and spread of hobgoblin garrisons, easing the pressure on our central administration and ensuring that our Great Command could govern the dishonourable peoples of Haless with greater efficiency than before.

player_overview.avoid_if: Avoid it if you prefer peaceful development, short campaigns or light administration, or dislike assimilation and enslavement narratives, late-game checklists and managing multiple systems.
player_overview.how_it_plays: Organise mine subjects and the three armies, then choose regional campaigns around resources and truces. Establish three new Commands, spread Wuhyun culture and reform administration before handling civil war, the shaman crisis and continental conquest.
player_overview.overview: The Command is Haless's already-running war machine in 1444. Choose 25 regional campaigns in the war room, balance six Commands, use Korashi to suppress magic and bring conquered peoples into the Wuhyun order. Its armies and starting base are formidable, but sustained conquest, the Rise of the Shamans and the Great Insubordination continually test your governance.
player_overview.recommended_for: Experienced players who enjoy strong openings, continuous warfare, dynamic missions, estate politics, imperial administration and major disasters.
signature_features: Dynamically choose 25 regional campaigns through the war room in an exceptionally long modular tree.
Manage the estates, factions and loyalty of the Wolf, Boar, Lion, Tiger, Elephant and Dragon Commands.
Maintain Korashi reserves to suppress magic and survive the Rise of the Shamans and Great Insubordination.
player_overview.tagline: Forge three hobgoblin Commands into an empire sweeping Haless, then prove who deserves to give orders during its most dangerous rebellion.

reasons: The war room turns the tree into selectable regional campaigns, allowing freer replay order.
Six Commands provide military identity, estate politics and a story of imperial reform.
Korashi, the Rise of the Shamans and the Great Insubordination give even this powerful state clear failure risks.
The three-Command alliance's transformation into the Supreme Command forms a vast, continuous national arc.
warnings: 215 direct missions and the 350-province endgame threshold mean a very long territorial checklist.
Six-Command loyalty, subjects, resources and disaster preparation impose a high management burden.
Forced assimilation, slave states and anti-magic persecution are core narrative content.
The entry verifies core mechanics, not every condition and reward of all 215 missions.

positive_indicators: Some conquered people can advance through the Wuhyun system
values.rationale: Slave subjects, bound spellcasters, institutional anti-magic persecution and forced identity remaking are the principal negatives; continental conquest itself is not counted again.
